In the museum, my Chinese friend told me an interesting story about
calligraphy. Wang Xizhi (303-361) was one of the best calligraphers in
history. He once attended a party of the Orchid Pavilion. Every guest was
expected to write a poem during the party. At the end of the party, Wang
wrote the introduction to the poems. The next day, Wang looked at his
calligraphy—the Lanting Xu lIntroduction to the poems written at the Orchid
Pavilion) —and realized that it was his best calligraphy ever. He then tried
to recreate the exact style of calligraphy, but he found it impossible to do
so. When he was at the party, he was very happy and relaxed. This made
his calligraphy especially lively. People later said that the calligraphy in the
Lanting Xu looked like a Chinese dragon at play.

The Yangize River and Its Guardians
Every morning, 53-year-old Chen Ming 0]
walks 15 kilometres along the Yangtze; wentifying causes and effects

River. As he does so, he often stops to | words and phrases, such as
talk to the people picnicking beside the | becouse, because of, as a result,
water or to watch the birds catch fishin so, etc.to signal causes and
the river’s clear water. While one might
think that he is just out for exercise, he is actually working. Mr Chen is a
“Guardian of the River" His job is to walk along the river and make sure
that no one is fishing in it or polluting it.
Mr Chen was not a “Guardian of the River” before. He grew up on the
banks of the Yangtze River and used to be a fisherman, like his father.
Back then, parts of the river were smelly and yellow because of the
waste from factories and homes. Fishermen were also catching too
many fish. As a result, the number of fish and plants in the river was
dropping quickly.
The government took action to deal with the problem before it was
too late. New waste centres were built to clean the wastewater before
it went into the river. Laws were made to stop new factories from being
built near the river. Boats were sent out to clean up the rubbish. Finally,
fishing was banned in the Yangtze River for 10 years from 2020. Mr
Chen and other fishermen were given new jobs as guardians to protect
the river. — i ” :

Good morning, students, teachers, and guests. Welcome to our junior high
graduation ceremony! To begin with, I would like to congratulate all the
new graduates. You have worked a long time for this moment. I remember
meeting you when you first came here, full of energy and curiosity. Today,
I’m full of pride as I see a room filled with talented youths, full of hope for
the future.
As you set out on your life’s new journey, first, I would like to say, find your
passion, and follow your dream! Find what you really love and put all your
energy and effort into it. Turn your eyes to the stats and keep your feet on
the ground.
Second, never give up! After graduation, everybody will be entering different
schools. No matter where you go, you will face new challenges. See every
challenge as an opportunity: an opportunity to grow, to learn, and to
succeed. So be brave and deal with your challenges through hard work.
Always bear in mind: Diligence leads to success in one’s life. Hard work will
not fail you.
Third, learn to be thankful. While you have worked hard to finish junior
high school, you did not work alone. Many others have lent hands to help
you, and they have worked equally hard to get you to this moment. These
people—your parents, teachers, and friends—have helped make you who
